instruction:
Run `C:\Users\user\Desktop\complex_stim.cir` together with `C:\Users\user\Desktop\complex_stim.stl` in native PSpice. Use the native PSpice command-line simulator `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\psp_cmd.exe`. For this workflow, use `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\Capture.exe` for OrCAD schematics and `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\allegro.exe` for board work.

Save the native simulator output as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\complex_stim.out`, then write `C:\Users\user\Desktop\stim_samples.json` with `tau_ms`, `R_ohms`, `C_F`, and a `segments` array. The four segments must be in the native sample-time order 1 ms, 3 ms, 6 ms, and 8 ms, with names `exp_rise`, `constant_3V`, `sine_on_DC`, and `pulse_train`, respectively. Each segment must include `name`, `t_sample_s` (in seconds), `V_in`, and `V_out`.
